hook.en: In a steel plant over a hundred years ago, F.W. Taylor timed men shovelling coal and found that the right shovel could nearly triple their output. That curiosity gave us scientific management.

body.en: Scientific management means knowing exactly what you want people to do and seeing that they do it in the best and cheapest way. F.W. Taylor, an American engineer, developed it to replace rule of thumb with methods found by scientific study.

points.en: Replaces guesswork with observation and experiment

title.en: On the board: Taylor's four principles

narration.en: Watch the board as we build this up step by step.

say.en: Taylor gave four principles. I will write each as "this, not that".
Science, not rule of thumb: find the one best way of doing each job.
Harmony, not discord: managers and workers must be partners. Taylor called this a mental revolution.
Cooperation, not individualism: share work and reward workers' suggestions.
Development of each person to the greatest efficiency and prosperity, through scientific selection and training.

explanation.en: Taylor wanted scientific methods, harmony and cooperation between management and workers, and the full development of every worker.

right.en: Study the best way to load a truck instead of guessing
A mental revolution: both sides stop fighting over profit and work to raise it
Management rewards workers' suggestions and shares responsibility
Select workers scientifically and train them in the best method

body.en: Harmony requires a complete mental revolution: management and workers stop fighting over the division of profit and work together to increase it. Development means selecting workers scientifically, giving them work that suits them and training them to be efficient.

points.en: Grow the cake instead of fighting over its share

narration.en: Science, Harmony, Cooperation, Development: S-H-C-D. Each is written as "this, not that".

problem.en: In a Peenya auto-parts unit, workers are paid poorly while owners keep all the gains, and both sides blame each other. A consultant asks them to sit together, share productivity gains and accept worker suggestions. Which principles of Taylor are being applied?

steps.en: Ending the blame game and becoming partners: Harmony, not discord (mental revolution).
Sharing work and rewarding suggestions: Cooperation, not individualism.
Sharing productivity gains supports development and prosperity of each worker.

answer.en: Harmony, not discord, and Cooperation, not individualism (with development of each person).
